title: Grateful Dead Live at Capitol Theater on 1970-11-08
source: Audience - Marty Weinberg and Ken Lee

ai_review.summary: Acoustic set with stellar banter and a phenomenal 'Going Down the Road', but the existing mono/distorted mix limits listening – a newer stereo restoration is recommended.
ai_review.review: The show shines with an acoustic opener, great setlist choices and memorable on‑stage chatter (the Godzilla story after Dark Hollow), plus what many call the sickest version ever of "Going Down the Road". However, the available recording suffers from a distorted mono mix that feels more archival than musical, prompting listeners to seek out the newer stereo restoration from the master tapes.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviewers rave about the performance (average 4.7★) but criticize the audio quality (average 2.5★). Weighted 70% show + 30% recording yields ~3.8★.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Distorted, mono mix; lacks stereo separation and clarity; described as archival rather than a clean soundboard capture. A newer stereo restoration from the master tapes is recommended.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Acoustic set followed by an NRPS set and then full Dead sets; banter between songs (e.g., Godzilla conversation) adds charm and keeps the momentum lively.
